errorCodes.meaning: No context with this id is reachable by the caller.
The context still holds keys, DIDs or templates and `force` was not set.

The published log of at least one `did:webvh` DID in the subtree could not be confirmed removed from its hosting server, and `abandonHostCopies` was not set. Nothing was deleted locally. Retry once the host is back, or retry with `abandonHostCopies` to complete the deletion and take on removing the named logs.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

daemonCleanupErrors.description: One entry per `did:webvh` DID in the deleted subtree whose local record was removed while its hosting server did not confirm removal of the published log. **Those DIDs may still resolve.** Only ever present when the request set `abandonHostCopies`; a requester that did not is refused instead. A consumer MUST surface it rather than treating the deletion as complete. Absent or empty means every host copy was confirmed gone.

deleted.description: Whether the context was removed. A successful response carrying `false` means the VTA declined to act — it is not an error, and a consumer MUST NOT report the deletion as done on the basis of the response status alone.

daemonCleanupErrors.description: One entry per `did:webvh` DID in the deleted subtree whose local record was removed while its hosting server did not confirm removal of the published log. **Those DIDs may still resolve.** Only ever present when the request set `abandonHostCopies`; a requester that did not is refused instead. A consumer MUST surface it rather than treating the deletion as complete. Absent or empty means every host copy was confirmed gone.

deleted.description: Whether the context was removed. A successful response carrying `false` means the VTA declined to act — it is not an error, and a consumer MUST NOT report the deletion as done on the basis of the response status alone.

abandonHostCopies.description: Complete the deletion even where the published log of a `did:webvh` DID in the subtree could not be confirmed removed from its hosting server — the server unreachable, refusing, or no longer known to the VTA. Default false: such a deletion is refused with `vta/contexts/delete:hostCleanupFailed` and nothing is deleted locally, so the caller can wait for the host and retry. True accepts that the named DIDs may keep resolving and that removing them is now the caller's responsibility; each is reported in `daemonCleanupErrors`.

force.description: Delete even though the context still holds keys, DIDs or templates. Default false, and the default is the point: without it a context holding anything is refused, so the destructive case is always something a caller asked for explicitly.
